subject.title: fix(ollama): stop oversized stream records from growing memory

question: Should native Ollama streaming reject every individual NDJSON response record larger than 16 MiB?
rationale: The limit directly fixes unbounded buffering but deliberately makes a previously accepted response shape fail closed, and neither the upstream protocol nor existing OpenClaw configuration establishes 16 MiB as the canonical maximum.

options.title: Confirm 16 MiB
options.body: Accept the fixed per-record boundary after the branch is refreshed and the production-path proof passes against current `main`.

options.title: Choose a shared limit
options.body: Replace the local constant with an established repository-wide bounded-response limit if maintainers identify one.

options.title: Request compatibility data
options.body: Pause until representative large Ollama responses establish a different safe maximum.

recommendation.title: Confirm 16 MiB
recommendation.body: Accept the fixed per-record boundary after the branch is refreshed and the production-path proof passes against current `main`.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the native Ollama stream parser and are the strongest feature-history owner for its response compatibility contract.
